boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Baxter Springs record (October 6, 1863) in Occupation of Indian Territory North of the Arkansas River [October 1863]. Quantrill's march south from Lafayette County and the killing of captives on the way to the Canadian are context. The killing of surrendered soldiers, bandsmen and civilians is recorded as reported, not as ordinary combat casualties. Campaign-wide marches, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Detachments from three regiments and an escort [US] and Quantrill's Raiders (approx. 400) [CS], and the frozen CS bound is 400; the live field reads 400 (US 0; CS 400). Britton says Quantrill marched with between three and four hundred men, that Blunt's escort was about one hundred, that about 150 mounted men formed on the escort's flank, that the escort thought itself attacked by not less than six hundred, and that less than a company of colored infantry was at the post. Quantrill says he took three companies, 150 men, to the prairie, found an escort of 125, and charged with 250 men.
claims.rationale: Estimates of an irregular force and escort counts at different moments; the escort's six hundred is an impression under attack. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live US zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Confederate victory and the live result Confederate Victory. Britton says the post held and Pond refused a summons, while Blunt's escort and band were destroyed on the prairie; Quantrill says he left only about 40 of the escort alive and did not renew the attack on the fort.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The label covers two distinct fights with opposite local outcomes.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 106 total (US 103; CS 3), as does the live field. Britton gives the Federal loss as three officers, sixty-seven enlisted men and ten citizens killed and eighteen wounded, says most of the escort's dead were shot through the head, that soldiers who surrendered were shot down, and that the fourteen bandsmen and others were murdered; he relays Pond's report of eleven raiders left dead. Quantrill gives his loss as 3 killed and 3 wounded in both fights, claims about 80 of the escort and 16 at the fort killed, naming Blunt, Henning and Tough among the dead although Britton places all three alive after the fight, and says of about 150 Union Indians and Black men caught on the march south that none were brought through.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Killings of surrendered men and civilians are recorded as reported and are not ordinary combat categories; captives killed on the later march belong to a separate event and are not added.

open_questions: Blunt's report (No. 1, read at its opening), Blair's and Henning's reports (Nos. 2-3), Pond's report (No. 4, read and not selected; a fourth family for this record) and any nominal list of the dead remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam's, 1899) is a retrospective history described on its title page as based upon official reports and the author's observations; it relays figures from Union and Confederate reports, so it is not independent of the Official Records families, and is treated as partly a participant's interested Union account. Quantrill's October 13, 1863 report to Price is one family of interested guerrilla accounts. Pond's report (No. 4) was read and not selected, to keep the record within three families. Official Records Series I, Volume XXII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
